# Automatic standalone four-deck bridge

This beta pairs the XDJ-XZ 1.26 runtime with a RAM-only USB helper and GPL-2.0-only hub module. Connect the rear USB-B socket directly to either top USB port. Music is optional when the audio route starts. Connect music drives directly to the other top port, or through one high-speed USB 2.0 hub in that port. These arrangements require separate physical-controller acceptance for each rebuilt package.

The helper selects the loopback top port from the exact XZ hub identity and topology. It retains that port and the controller boot identity for its lifetime. A bounded inventory verifies music mount records and their physical ancestry on the opposite port, allowing one external hub. Music can arrive after the audio route starts. Invalid or changing inventory cannot authorize a bind. Moving the loopback cable to the other top port requires restarting the USB loader; an active helper never retargets the module.

The module requires the read-only parameter `loopback_port=1` or `loopback_port=2`. Missing or invalid selection fails before notifier registration. The selected port accepts only the exact XZ loopback hub. With `music_hubs=1`, the opposite top port also admits one high-speed, single-interface music hub. Both adoption paths require an unbound, childless hub with a retained CONFIGURED or SUSPENDED configuration under the exact onboard hub. Direct storage devices, already-bound hubs, the onboard hub and cascaded hubs are not modified.

The module changes volatile hub metadata only. The helper performs explicit driver binds while native decks are stopped, after rechecking device generation and module ownership. Each admitted hub holds its own device reference and module pin. Physical disconnection restores that hub's original metadata and releases its references; a configured driver unbind alone does not count as physical disconnection. There is no forced unload.

The helper retains the exact application/runtime, receiver, kernel ABI, RAM-path and process checks. Boot identity is observed, never supplied by the caller. Mounted media must pass the filesystem and physical-ancestry checks. FAT16/FAT32, exFAT, HFS+/HFSX and later-partition validation remain in place. Serial absence is recorded explicitly rather than replaced with an invented identity. Legacy diagnostic IDs containing `USB2` remain readable, but their checks follow the selected music port.

Execution remains under the USB loader. The bootstrap stages the helper, module and runtime under `/dev/shm`. No firmware installation, persistent boot change or music-drive write is introduced by the bridge. Keep a drive connected while a track is being read from it. A music hub does not add native source buttons or guarantee that the stock firmware exposes every attached drive.

The Windows package includes licenses/xz-hub-source.tar.gz with the complete retained kernel source, configuration, local compiler compatibility header, module and build recipes. The same archive accompanies the beta release. Extract it into a fresh directory and run bash build-module.sh using ARM GNU EABI GCC13, GNU binutils, make and Python3. CRCs are derived from recompiling source; live CRC substitution is not used. The kernel build directory is disposable.

build_bridge.py accepts --payload, --module, --sha-source, --zig and --output. Supply your locally prepared supported application/runtime payload, the built module directory and mods/audio/vendor/sha256. It derives exact hashes/ABI pins and compiles a staged source copy against that generated contract, then checks the ARM32 GLIBC2.4 build with QEMU. Rebuilding a helper/module requires refreshing the USB-loader resource and bootstrap hashes together; existing packaged bytes remain pinned. Proprietary firmware, application binaries and boot keys are not included in corresponding source.

`verify_binding.py --output SCRATCH [--arm]` runs the helper against in-memory filesystem/process fixtures with live operations forbidden. `bash verify-module.sh SCRATCH` runs both port orientations under host ASan/UBSan, ARM/QEMU and host TSan, including ownership, invalid selection, notifier races and physical-disconnect cleanup. Each command requires a new scratch directory outside the source tree.

detach.S is GPL-2.0-only and builds with arm-linux-gnueabi-gcc -nostdlib -static -no-pie -march=armv7-a -marm -Wl,--build-id=none detach.S -o detach. The bridge is MIT-licensed; its SHA256 implementation retains its own public-domain notice under mods/audio/vendor/sha256.

Offline lifecycle and sanitizer tests plus exact on-device read-only qualification do not establish audible playback, kernel scheduling under every workload or complete four-deck performance acceptance. The beta release notes list remaining limitations.
